title: Equity Outcome Map
captions:
WEBVTT

00:02.200 --> 00:04.245
An ordinary decision can change someone's

00:04.280 --> 00:06.665
experience of government. A notice or a program

00:06.700 --> 00:08.805
requirement can open a door, or make it

00:08.840 --> 00:10.705
harder to get through. At the Minnesota

00:10.740 --> 00:12.845
Department of Human Services, everyday choices

00:12.880 --> 00:15.040
are part of the equity story.

00:15.240 --> 00:18.625
The Equity Outcome Map for 2025 through 2026

00:18.660 --> 00:20.965
asks how those choices can add up to

00:21.000 --> 00:22.785
something better: services that meet

00:22.820 --> 00:25.145
Minnesotans' needs, and a workplace where people

00:25.180 --> 00:27.225
can contribute and build a career.

00:27.260 --> 00:29.120
Here is how the map took shape.

00:31.570 --> 00:34.495
In fall 2025, the Office of Strategy and

00:34.530 --> 00:36.495
Performance partnered with the Office of

00:36.530 --> 00:39.135
Innovation and Impact and the Office of Employee

00:39.170 --> 00:42.810
Culture. Their inquiry looked across the
department.

00:43.010 --> 00:45.575
The question was practical. What is already

00:45.610 --> 00:48.015
helping equity become part of everyday work?

00:48.050 --> 00:49.815
Where does progress get stuck?

00:49.850 --> 00:51.735
Understanding both would matter before deciding

00:51.770 --> 00:54.170
what to strengthen or change.

00:54.370 --> 00:56.635
The team reviewed more than 25 documents,

00:56.670 --> 00:58.675
dashboards, and webpages, and held 34

00:58.710 --> 01:01.415
interviews. Written plans showed one part of the

01:01.450 --> 01:03.795
picture. People's perspectives helped explain

01:03.830 --> 01:06.250
the conditions surrounding that work.

01:08.700 --> 01:11.725
The inquiry unfolded in four connected phases,

01:11.760 --> 01:13.425
moving from an initial picture toward deeper

01:13.460 --> 01:17.380
understanding, and then a chance to shape the
work together.

01:17.580 --> 01:19.985
An initial meeting and document review began in

01:20.020 --> 01:22.945
September 2025, establishing a starting point

01:22.980 --> 01:26.020
for understanding the department's equity work.

01:26.220 --> 01:29.045
Interviews and deeper document review followed.

01:29.080 --> 01:31.465
Analysis then brought those materials together,

01:31.500 --> 01:33.285
looking for connections between the work people

01:33.320 --> 01:36.420
described and the barriers they encountered.

01:36.620 --> 01:39.305
In April 2026, the findings moved into

01:39.340 --> 01:41.885
co-creation. The next question became how to

01:41.920 --> 01:44.980
turn what had been learned into a shared
direction.

01:47.430 --> 01:50.155
Thirty-four people contributed perspectives from

01:50.190 --> 01:54.350
different parts of DHS, bringing several views
into the inquiry.

01:54.550 --> 01:56.855
Eleven participants came from Innovation and

01:56.890 --> 01:59.315
Impact, four from Diversity Recruitment and

01:59.350 --> 02:03.310
Retention, and four from the Office of Employee
Culture.

02:03.510 --> 02:05.995
Another nine came from A D S A,

02:06.030 --> 02:08.095
B H A and H S S A,

02:08.130 --> 02:11.790
H C A, O I G, and Operations.

02:11.990 --> 02:14.315
Six more came from Tribal and Urban Indian

02:14.350 --> 02:16.951
Relations, Community Relations, and the C E C

02:16.986 --> 02:19.315
L C, adding relationship and community

02:19.350 --> 02:21.870
perspectives to the picture.

02:24.320 --> 02:26.805
Across this work, six principles provide a

02:26.840 --> 02:29.205
shared compass. Equitably serving all

02:29.240 --> 02:31.465
Minnesotans keeps the purpose in view:

02:31.500 --> 02:34.280
the people affected by the department's
decisions.

02:34.480 --> 02:36.705
Transparency and trust, along with mutual

02:36.740 --> 02:39.665
respect and psychological safety, create room to

02:39.700 --> 02:43.080
raise a concern and hear a different
perspective.

02:43.280 --> 02:45.545
Continuous learning and accountability connect

02:45.580 --> 02:48.405
reflection with responsibility. Stability and

02:48.440 --> 02:51.285
sustainability keep attention on lasting work.

02:51.320 --> 02:52.885
And the final principle, we are stronger

02:52.920 --> 02:56.520
together, ties those commitments to
collaboration.

02:58.970 --> 03:01.795
The interviews also described barriers.

03:01.830 --> 03:03.915
A shared aspiration alone cannot remove the

03:03.950 --> 03:05.970
conditions that get in its way.

03:06.170 --> 03:08.875
Participants identified unclear roles, work

03:08.910 --> 03:11.855
culture, systemic racism, and silos.

03:11.890 --> 03:14.035
Limited access to data, stretched staffing, and

03:14.070 --> 03:18.050
limited time could make it harder to understand
a problem or act on it.

03:18.250 --> 03:20.715
They also described superficial community

03:20.750 --> 03:23.675
engagement, turnover, gaps in accountability,

03:23.710 --> 03:26.450
the political climate, and uneven training.

03:26.650 --> 03:29.015
Another concern ran through the picture:

03:29.050 --> 03:31.115
equity could be treated as an add-on, without

03:31.150 --> 03:33.455
a shared understanding of what it means.

03:33.490 --> 03:37.090
The map responds by connecting equity to the
work itself.

03:39.540 --> 03:42.045
That connection becomes a theory of change:

03:42.080 --> 03:43.645
how better conditions and different choices

03:43.680 --> 03:45.865
might contribute to better outcomes.

03:45.900 --> 03:48.300
It gives the work a direction to test.

03:48.500 --> 03:50.965
The starting condition is that DHS centers

03:51.000 --> 03:52.725
equity throughout its work and operations,

03:52.760 --> 03:57.500
including policies, contracts, training, and
performance plans.

03:57.700 --> 03:59.985
The intended result is that Minnesotans receive

04:00.020 --> 04:02.285
the services they need, without disparities in

04:02.320 --> 04:04.565
access and experience, and can live their

04:04.600 --> 04:07.085
healthiest, fullest lives. These are ambitions

04:07.120 --> 04:09.180
the work must help advance.

04:09.380 --> 04:11.645
The same theory looks inward:

04:11.680 --> 04:13.665
DHS would become an inclusive employer where all

04:13.700 --> 04:15.345
people can build a career.

04:15.380 --> 04:19.100
Neither result is automatic; progress must be
examined.

04:21.550 --> 04:24.215
The outcome map puts the pieces together.

04:24.250 --> 04:26.295
Policy and strategy give direction.

04:26.330 --> 04:28.495
Activities turn that direction into work people

04:28.530 --> 04:31.030
can recognize and take part in.

04:31.230 --> 04:33.575
Those activities include workforce and hiring,

04:33.610 --> 04:36.215
learning, data, engagement, integrity, and

04:36.250 --> 04:38.755
collaboration. Communication, meetings,

04:38.790 --> 04:40.895
workgroups, and resources help people carry the

04:40.930 --> 04:43.590
work across organizational boundaries.

04:43.790 --> 04:45.775
The connections point toward four intended

04:45.810 --> 04:48.255
outcomes. How might an activity improve

04:48.290 --> 04:51.750
someone's experience, and what would show
whether it does?

04:54.200 --> 04:56.925
First is centering equity for DHS:

04:56.960 --> 04:59.365
making it part of everyday work, sustaining it

04:59.400 --> 05:00.985
through leadership changes, and creating

05:01.020 --> 05:02.845
conditions where staff can bring themselves to

05:02.880 --> 05:05.040
work while building their careers.

05:05.240 --> 05:08.165
Second is centering equity for Minnesotans.

05:08.200 --> 05:09.505
The aim is for public funds to reach

05:09.540 --> 05:11.365
the adults and children who need them most,

05:11.400 --> 05:14.800
while health disparities are reduced or
eliminated.

05:15.000 --> 05:17.585
Third is a continuous learning cycle.

05:17.620 --> 05:19.905
Staff would feel safe receiving feedback, and

05:19.940 --> 05:21.925
leaders at every level would hold themselves and

05:21.960 --> 05:24.045
others accountable. Learning would lead to a

05:24.080 --> 05:26.640
response, then further learning.

05:26.840 --> 05:29.425
Fourth is centering community: culturally

05:29.460 --> 05:31.965
responsible engagement, language access, and

05:32.000 --> 05:33.885
community participation built into program

05:33.920 --> 05:36.865
design. The aspiration is for that relationship

05:36.900 --> 05:39.520
to shape the work as it develops.

05:41.970 --> 05:44.755
Consider an illustrative example: a team is

05:44.790 --> 05:46.935
revising a service notice. It could ask who

05:46.970 --> 05:49.255
may have difficulty understanding it, listen to

05:49.290 --> 05:52.810
affected people, and use that learning to
improve the notice.

05:53.010 --> 05:55.295
The map identifies support through employee

05:55.330 --> 05:57.495
resource groups, community engagement and

05:57.530 --> 06:00.195
feedback loops, equity forums, retreats, and

06:00.230 --> 06:04.650
Tribal consultations, each serving its own
purpose and relationships.

06:04.850 --> 06:07.315
It also includes using data to close workforce

06:07.350 --> 06:09.455
gaps, embedding equity in hiring and

06:09.490 --> 06:11.375
contracting, and building learning through

06:11.410 --> 06:13.770
training and Equity Week.

06:13.970 --> 06:16.615
Practical resources include the Equity Analysis

06:16.650 --> 06:19.235
Toolkit, an integrity tip line, and shared

06:19.270 --> 06:22.015
equity language. The useful next step is to

06:22.050 --> 06:25.690
connect the right resource to a real decision or
concern.

06:28.140 --> 06:30.965
The map identifies measures for each outcome,

06:31.000 --> 06:35.060
helping examine progress and where people still
experience barriers.

06:35.260 --> 06:37.285
Measures include retention and career

06:37.320 --> 06:39.705
advancement rates, completion and scores for the

06:39.740 --> 06:41.825
Intercultural Development Inventory, use of the

06:41.860 --> 06:43.885
Equity Analysis Toolkit, and decisions

06:43.920 --> 06:47.940
co-created with community. Each offers part of
the picture.

06:48.140 --> 06:50.325
Wherever possible, the measures are examined by

06:50.360 --> 06:53.485
race and ethnicity, gender, division, and staff

06:53.520 --> 06:56.225
or manager. Looking beneath an overall result

06:56.260 --> 06:59.700
can reveal differences that would otherwise be
easy to miss.

07:02.150 --> 07:03.995
The map brings us back to the everyday

07:04.030 --> 07:07.790
decision, and the person whose experience it may
change.

07:08.090 --> 07:09.695
Start with a piece of work in front

07:09.730 --> 07:13.250
of you. Name the outcome it is meant to support.

07:13.550 --> 07:15.915
Consider whose perspective is needed, and how

07:15.950 --> 07:18.310
those people can help shape the decision.

07:18.610 --> 07:20.795
Use the available evidence, listen for what it

07:20.830 --> 07:23.050
misses, and make room to learn.

07:23.350 --> 07:25.095
Then return to the outcome.

07:25.130 --> 07:29.390
Examine what changed, what did not, and what
deserves another look.

07:29.690 --> 07:33.555
For directors, managers, supervisors, and staff,

07:33.590 --> 07:35.355
this map is the shared foundation for

07:35.390 --> 07:37.855
equity-related learning and practice in One DHS

07:37.890 --> 07:40.935
and One DSD People, Access and Culture.

07:40.970 --> 07:42.515
The work continues through decisions,

07:42.550 --> 07:46.450
relationships, and follow-through. We are
stronger together.

title: People, Access and Culture in Practice: A Disability Services Division Example
captions:
WEBVTT

00:02.200 --> 00:04.385
A person opens a letter about support at

00:04.420 --> 00:06.905
home. A new colleague begins work.

00:06.940 --> 00:09.005
A team prepares a recommendation.

00:09.040 --> 00:11.225
Each moment raises the same question:

00:11.260 --> 00:12.905
will this decision make it easier for people

00:12.940 --> 00:15.280
to participate and get what they need?

00:15.480 --> 00:17.685
People, Access and Culture connects those

00:17.720 --> 00:20.485
moments. These illustrative situations draw on

00:20.520 --> 00:23.325
Disability Services Division work. They show how

00:23.360 --> 00:25.525
the Equity Outcome Map can guide practice across

00:25.560 --> 00:29.200
DHS, with One DSD as a worked example.

00:31.650 --> 00:34.455
The map describes four intended outcomes:

00:34.490 --> 00:37.555
centering equity for DHS, centering equity for

00:37.590 --> 00:40.035
Minnesotans, a continuous learning cycle, and

00:40.070 --> 00:41.530
centering community.

00:41.730 --> 00:44.015
Its six guiding principles describe how to

00:44.050 --> 00:45.530
pursue that work.

00:45.730 --> 00:47.555
The Aging and Disability Services

00:47.590 --> 00:49.715
Administration's six implementation goals

00:49.750 --> 00:52.995
identify areas for action. Outcomes, principles,

00:53.030 --> 00:55.255
and implementation goals play different parts.

00:55.290 --> 00:57.055
A single improvement can support more than one

00:57.090 --> 00:58.330
outcome.

01:00.780 --> 01:02.825
The first three goals are Eliminate Disparities,

01:02.860 --> 01:06.340
Community Engagement, and Hiring and Retention.

01:06.540 --> 01:08.705
The next three are Learning and Development,

01:08.740 --> 01:10.965
Contracts and Procurement, and Communication and

01:11.000 --> 01:12.420
Accessibility.

01:12.620 --> 01:15.065
Together, they connect people's experiences with

01:15.100 --> 01:17.545
decisions about services, relationships,

01:17.580 --> 01:19.725
employees, and resources. Let's follow that

01:19.760 --> 01:21.940
connection into the work.

01:24.390 --> 01:28.615
Community First Services and Supports, or CFSS,

01:28.650 --> 01:30.535
offers support for independence at home and in

01:30.570 --> 01:32.575
the community. Imagine someone reading

01:32.610 --> 01:34.495
information about moving to this program and

01:34.530 --> 01:36.350
wondering what to do next.

01:36.550 --> 01:39.615
The team checks the current official guidance.

01:39.650 --> 01:41.475
Then it asks people who use services what

01:41.510 --> 01:43.995
is unclear, what format they need, and where

01:44.030 --> 01:45.630
they would turn for help.

01:48.080 --> 01:50.345
Using the Equity Analysis Toolkit,

01:50.380 --> 01:52.685
plain-language guidance, and the National CLAS

01:52.720 --> 01:54.645
Standards for culturally and linguistically

01:54.680 --> 01:57.305
appropriate services, the team revises the

01:57.340 --> 02:00.245
information. One DSD's language-access resources

02:00.280 --> 02:02.065
help it explain the next step and where

02:02.100 --> 02:04.205
to get assistance, without promising a decision

02:04.240 --> 02:05.640
it cannot make.

02:05.840 --> 02:08.185
Community Engagement and Communication and

02:08.220 --> 02:10.105
Accessibility support the goal to Eliminate

02:10.140 --> 02:13.405
Disparities. The result question is concrete:

02:13.440 --> 02:15.285
can people understand the next step and obtain

02:15.320 --> 02:17.445
help, including those whose needs the first

02:17.480 --> 02:19.160
version overlooked?

02:21.610 --> 02:24.275
Now consider MnCHOICES. Counties, Tribal

02:24.310 --> 02:26.855
nations, and managed care organizations use it

02:26.890 --> 02:28.675
in assessment and support planning for people

02:28.710 --> 02:31.155
who need long-term services and supports.

02:31.190 --> 02:32.995
The conversation should begin with the person's

02:33.030 --> 02:35.490
preferences and the life they want.

02:35.690 --> 02:37.735
In our example, someone leaves a planning

02:37.770 --> 02:39.695
conversation unsure which supports were

02:39.730 --> 02:41.615
discussed or whom to contact.

02:41.650 --> 02:42.915
The question is how to make that next

02:42.950 --> 02:44.815
step clearer while keeping the person's choices

02:44.850 --> 02:46.450
central.

02:48.900 --> 02:51.105
The team uses person-centered learning and

02:51.140 --> 02:53.145
collaboration resources to clarify the

02:53.180 --> 02:56.005
explanation and handoff. Disability Hub

02:56.040 --> 02:58.045
Minnesota can help people explore options and

02:58.080 --> 03:00.385
find information; eligibility and service

03:00.420 --> 03:03.500
decisions remain with the responsible agencies.

03:03.700 --> 03:05.965
Staff check back: does the person understand

03:06.000 --> 03:08.365
their options and know where to turn?

03:08.400 --> 03:10.285
That connects community participation and

03:10.320 --> 03:12.345
learning with access, rather than counting a

03:12.380 --> 03:15.020
referral as a successful outcome.

03:17.470 --> 03:19.755
A different team is considering a contract for

03:19.790 --> 03:22.015
provider training and technical assistance.

03:22.050 --> 03:23.995
This is an illustrative purchasing decision,

03:24.030 --> 03:26.735
separate from Medicaid provider enrollment or an

03:26.770 --> 03:28.630
individual's services.

03:28.830 --> 03:31.035
Using the contracting learning resources and

03:31.070 --> 03:33.635
Equity Analysis Toolkit, staff examine the

03:33.670 --> 03:36.275
proposed scope, outreach, and accessibility.

03:36.310 --> 03:38.035
Could capable organizations learn about the

03:38.070 --> 03:40.475
opportunity and understand what is needed?

03:40.510 --> 03:42.215
The responsible procurement colleagues review

03:42.250 --> 03:44.070
proposed changes.

03:44.270 --> 03:46.515
Contracts and Procurement becomes a question

03:46.550 --> 03:49.355
about meaningful access and useful work:

03:49.390 --> 03:51.295
does the purchased assistance reach the people

03:51.330 --> 03:53.590
it is intended to support?

03:56.040 --> 03:59.045
Inside DSD, a new colleague needs more than

03:59.080 --> 04:01.765
a list of links. They need clear expectations,

04:01.800 --> 04:04.185
accessible materials, working relationships, and

04:04.220 --> 04:06.240
room to ask questions.

04:06.440 --> 04:08.865
A supervisor uses onboarding and collaboration

04:08.900 --> 04:11.745
resources to plan early conversations and

04:11.780 --> 04:14.345
relevant learning. Hiring and Retention connects

04:14.380 --> 04:16.905
with Learning and Development. Later, they ask

04:16.940 --> 04:19.305
whether the colleague can contribute, find help,

04:19.340 --> 04:21.545
and raise concerns. Finishing a course alone

04:21.580 --> 04:24.005
does not show that workplace conditions or

04:24.040 --> 04:25.680
retention improved.

04:28.130 --> 04:30.555
These same questions belong in policy,

04:30.590 --> 04:33.135
legislative, and bill analysis. Suppose a

04:33.170 --> 04:35.635
proposed waiver change could affect access.

04:35.670 --> 04:37.695
Staff distinguish the proposal from enacted law

04:37.730 --> 04:39.635
and current program guidance before describing

04:39.670 --> 04:41.130
what it would mean.

04:41.330 --> 04:43.635
The policy and legislative course and Equity

04:43.670 --> 04:45.835
Analysis Toolkit help them examine who may

04:45.870 --> 04:48.275
benefit, who may face barriers, and whose

04:48.310 --> 04:50.215
perspective is missing. Their recommendation

04:50.250 --> 04:52.395
explains the evidence, alternatives, and

04:52.430 --> 04:55.050
questions still requiring an answer.

04:57.500 --> 05:00.625
One DHS and One DSD People, Access and

05:00.660 --> 05:02.405
Culture bring relevant learning and practical

05:02.440 --> 05:05.085
resources together. Begin with work you actually

05:05.120 --> 05:07.505
need to do: improve a notice, prepare a

05:07.540 --> 05:09.605
recommendation, strengthen a partnership, or

05:09.640 --> 05:11.140
welcome a colleague.

05:11.340 --> 05:13.685
Choose learning at a useful depth, use the

05:13.720 --> 05:15.365
appropriate tool, and involve the people

05:15.400 --> 05:18.285
affected. The applications support that work;

05:18.320 --> 05:20.125
they do not replace official guidance or the

05:20.160 --> 05:22.500
people responsible for decisions.

05:24.950 --> 05:28.915
For directors, managers, supervisors, and staff,

05:28.950 --> 05:31.235
the connection is practical: choose an intended

05:31.270 --> 05:34.315
outcome, connect the relevant ADSA goal, and

05:34.350 --> 05:35.955
decide what to do next.

05:35.990 --> 05:38.235
Then ask what changed for people, what remains

05:38.270 --> 05:40.830
difficult, and what to learn together.

05:41.130 --> 05:43.475
That is how People, Access and Culture moves

05:43.510 --> 05:46.530
from a shared purpose into everyday practice.
